Matthew and Diane's sepsis story: Part 4 - The importance of adverse event reviews

In part four of this video series, Matthew Ames talks about visiting a range of health professionals before he was admitted to hospital. 
He believes had they had access to all of his health records, he may have been diagnosed with sepsis earlier.
Matthew says adverse events in New Zealand highlight there are issues around either making a diagnosis too early, making the wrong diagnosis, or diagnosing too late.

Matthew and Diane's sepsis story: Part 3 - Lessons learned and opportunities for improvement

In part three of this video series, Matthew Ames talks about waking from an induced coma and having his wife Diane share the news that his limbs had been amputated to save his life. 

Matthew and his wife Diane felt well supported by his healthcare team that day, and during his recovery and rehabilitation.

Matthew and Diane's sepsis story: Part 2 - Matthew's recovery

In part two of this video series, Matthew Ames' wife Diane talks about what happened when Matthew woke from his induced coma. 
Diane stepped him through what happened as his condition deteriorated, and the decision was made to amputate his limbs to save his life.

Matthew and Diane's sepsis story: Part 1 - Matthew's diagnosis

In part one of this video series, Matthew and Diane Ames speak about his diagnosis and treatment for sepsis. 

In 2013, the father of four experienced what he thought was a common sore throat. Over the course of a week he visited his local GP and hospital emergency department, being told each time that he had a viral illness. 

When his condition deteriorated he went back to the emergency department. He was admitted to hospital, where he was diagnosed with sepsis. 

Despite aggressive medical intervention, all of Matthew’s limbs had to be amputated to save his life. 

This video contains content and images that some people may find distressing.

Matthew and Diane's sepsis story (full length)

In 2013, 39-year-old father of four Matthew Ames experienced what he thought was a common sore throat. 

Over the course of a week he visited his local GP and hospital emergency department, being told on each time that he had a viral illness. 

When his condition deteriorated, he went back to the emergency department. He was admitted to hospital, where he was diagnosed with sepsis. 

Despite aggressive medical intervention, all of Matthew’s limbs had to be amputated to save his life.  

In this video, Matthew and his wife Diane share their story of his diagnosis, recovery, lessons learned from his experience, and the importance of adverse event reviews.  

This video contains content and images that some people may find distressing.

He Mapi Nā Tātou, Mō Tātou: A map by you, controlled by you. Build your Hapū GIS from scratch.

This is the first of two recorded hands-on wānanga showing you how to build your own hapū GIS project – from scratch, at no cost. It’s a practical step-by-step session, designed for beginners with little or no GIS experience.In this recording we cover:
✅ How to install and set up free desktop GIS software (Windows & MacOS)
✅ Where to download basemaps, LINZ parcels, Māori land blocks, awa, roto, maunga, and aerial imagery
✅ How to use the Ngā Poutama starter GIS kete to get clicking sooner
✅ Exploring layers of whenua data and saving/exporting simple maps to share with your whānauWe also provide a complete, ready-to-use GIS project for every rohe in Aotearoa. You can open and use the data offline on your own computer – your maps, your stories, your control.

Part two of this series (September 2025) goes further: creating your own data for sites of significance and other kaupapa Māori projects.Ngā mihi nui ki a koutou for joining this journey of digital whenua mapping.

Drone footage of Clarence River Avulsion

Aerial footage captured five years following the 2016 Kaikōura earthquake. A white vehicle sits atop the area uplifted by the Papatea fault, which caused the Waiau Toa / Clarence River to change course and flow along the base of the fault, forming a sprawling new braided river channel. 

Drone footage credit: Regine Morgenstern, ESNZ (2021).

Mahiwi Farm — Equity Partnership

Pāmu is proud to launch a new equity partnership opportunity that puts people at the centre of farm ownership and performance.

The first opportunity under this model is Mahiwi Farm, a 708 effective-hectare livestock property near Wairoa. This is more than just a farm — it’s a chance for one of our own to step into a leadership role with real equity, accountability, and the ability to shape the future of the land.

Mayor's Taskforce for Jobs Ruapehu

It’s tough out there. The Ruapehu District has been hit hard, and for young people trying to break into work, the struggle is even tougher. But some are fighting back. In Taumarunui, builder Rephan Woods is taking on 18-year-old apprentice Hoani Adams-Topine. With backing from the Mayor’s Taskforce for Jobs, they’re proving that local businesses and young people can build a future - together.  Thanks to James Towers and Louise McCoard from MTFJ for the work they do.

Crisis response webinar: what makes an effective crisis response - insights from a literature scan

Te Hiringa Mahara hosted a webinar on 25 September, 2025 showcasing findings from our Crisis response recent literature.

The webinar featured panellists offering real-world examples of effective crisis response practice. They discussed how different approaches can inform crisis responses that are timely, non-coercive, culturally safe and connected to wider systems of care.

Our panellists were:
• Sonya Russell, Kaiwhakahaere Hauora Hinengaro, Waranga | Director Mental Health and Addiction Sector Leadership, Te Hiringa Mahara – Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission
• Ruth Borrett, Chief Operating Officer, Ember Korowai Takitini
• Inspector Matt Morris, Health Partnerships Team Manager, Prevention Team, NZ Police.

The session was chaired by Dr Barbara Disley, Te Hiringa Mahara board member.

Read our recent literature scan here: https://www.mhwc.govt.nz/news-and-resources/crisis-response-literature-scan-downloads/

This webinar is part of the ongoing Te Hiringa Mahara programme of work on the crisis response system.
